title: This Comet From Another Solar System Is Full of Alcohol!
summary:
Imagine a giant snowball flying through space, and it's full of alcohol. That's kind of what comet 3I/ATLAS is like! This comet came from outside our solar system, and scientists just found out it has a LOT of methanol, which is a type of alcohol.

Comets are like icy time capsules from when planets formed. This one is special because it's only the third object we've ever seen come from interstellar space — that means from between the stars. The first two were called 'Oumuamua and Borisov.

Scientists used a giant telescope in Chile called ALMA to study 3I/ATLAS. They looked at the gases around the comet, called its coma. They found that the amount of methanol compared to another molecule, hydrogen cyanide, was super high. On two days, the ratio was about 70 and 120. That makes it one of the most methanol-rich comets ever studied!

But here's the cool part: the methanol isn't just coming from the comet's center. It's also coming from tiny ice grains floating around the comet. As the comet gets closer to the Sun, the ice grains heat up and release more methanol, like mini-comets!

Why does this matter? Because it tells us that comets in other solar systems might form differently than ours. Nathan Roth, a scientist who worked on the study, said, "Observing 3I/ATLAS is like taking a fingerprint from another solar system." Each comet tells us something new about how planets and moons are made. And this one is full of surprises!
why_it_matters: Finding out that a comet from outside our solar system is full of methanol helps scientists understand how planets and moons are made across the universe.

background_read: Comets are icy leftovers from the time when planets were forming, like icy time capsules.
3I/ATLAS came from interstellar space, meaning it did not start its journey in our solar system.
Only two interstellar visitors were known before 3I/ATLAS: 'Oumuamua and Borisov (the first two scientists ever identified from another star system).
Article_Structure: WHO: Nathan Roth and other scientists who studied 3I/ATLAS with the ALMA telescope.
WHAT: They discovered the comet is rich in methanol and that extra methanol also comes from tiny ice grains around the comet.
WHERE: On comet 3I/ATLAS in space, using the giant ALMA telescope in Chile.
WHY: Because 3I/ATLAS came from another solar system, studying its chemicals is like reading a fingerprint of how comets form there.

perspectives.perspective: The scientists who made the discovery
perspectives.description: They are excited because 3I/ATLAS is like a fingerprint from another solar system, and each new comet can change what we know about how planets form.

perspectives.perspective: Other astronomers who study distant objects
perspectives.description: They know that three interstellar visitors is a tiny sample, so one comet alone may not explain all the other solar systems in the universe.
It is amazing that scientists can learn so much about a faraway comet by studying the gases around it with a giant telescope.
